newsitem.title: UK: UK govt names outside monetary policy appointees.
newsitem.headline: UK govt names outside monetary policy appointees.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown on Monday appointed four outside members to the Bank of England's new monetary policy committee -- Professor Charles Goodhart, Dr DeAnne Julius, Sir Alan Budd and Professor Wilhelm Buiter.

The four will sit on the committee alongside four members from the Bank of England, led by by Governor Eddie George, until the appointment of a second deputy governor to the Bank takes its number to five.
The committee will meet for the first time to discuss interest rates on Thursday and Friday.
"I am delighted that we have secured the services of such distinguished individuals for the Monetary Policy Committee," Brown said.

"They will bring not only recognised expertise in their own fields, but a breadth of experience of finance and industry to the making of monetary policy in this country. Their appointments...will strengthen the Bank and enhance the credibility of monetary policy in Britain."

The new committee will be accountable to a reformed Court of the Bank of England. "In order to strengthen the capacity of the Court to exercise the role, Christopher Allsopp of Oxford University has been appointed...to join the Court," a Treasury statement said.
Brown will reaffirm the appointments once legislation to reform the monetary structure has been passed by Parliament.

Goodhart and Buiter will join the committee immediately. Julius' appointment will take effect from September 1 and Budd will be appointed by the Bank when he leaves his post as Chief Economic Adviser to the Treasury, the statement said.
Brown said all the necessary interim arrangements were now in place for the Bank to take on operational responsibility for setting interest rates.

"This radical reform to monetary policy decision-making will create a platform of stability and prudent economic management for the long-term which will allow Britain to achieve high levels of growth and employment."
